questions.q: What is the general solution to the ODE y'(t) = k*y(t)?
questions.explain: Separating variables (dy/y = k dt) and integrating gives ln|y| = kt + C, which exponentiates to y(t) = y0 * e^(kt).

questions.q: What is the purpose of the integrating factor μ(t) = e^(∫p(t)dt) when solving y' + p(t)y = q(t)?
options: It eliminates the need for any initial condition
It makes the left-hand side equal to the derivative of the product μ(t)y(t), which can then be integrated directly
It converts the ODE into an algebraic equation with no integration needed
questions.explain: Multiplying by μ(t) is chosen precisely so that d/dt[μ(t)y(t)] = μ(t)q(t), turning the ODE into something directly integrable.

questions.q: In the Vasicek model's deterministic equation r'(t) = a(b - r(t)), what does the solution r(t) = b + (r0 - b)e^(-at) describe?
options: The rate mean-reverting exponentially from r0 toward the long-run level b
The rate staying constant at r0 for all time
questions.explain: As t increases, e^(-at) decays to zero, so r(t) approaches b; the rate exponentially mean-reverts toward b at speed controlled by a.

questions.q: What is the update rule used in Euler's method for solving y' = f(t, y) numerically?
questions.explain: Euler's method takes a small step h in the direction of the derivative: y_(n+1) = y_n + h * f(t_n, y_n), directly from the definition of the derivative.

questions.q: What distinguishes a 'particular solution' of an ODE from the 'general solution'?
options: The particular solution has no free constants, pinned down by an initial condition like y(0) = y0
The particular solution is always a polynomial
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
The general solution requires numerical methods while the particular solution does not
questions.explain: The general solution contains a free constant; applying an initial condition pins that constant down to produce one specific, particular solution.
